Diff reviewed and every changed symbol traced repo-wide. Verified-clean items first, then findings.

**Verified clean (no breakage):**
- `getAnthropicClient` — zero remaining references anywhere (source, tests, `docs/`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `documentation/`). Rename is complete; both call sites (`/repo/app/lib/llm/callLlm.ts:133`, `/repo/app/lib/llm/streamLlm.ts:207`) updated.
- SSE consumer: the only client-side reader of the streaming endpoints is `/repo/app/lib/formalization/api.ts:89-94`, which reads `JSON.parse(dataStr).error` only and never touches `details`. `transformSseStream.ts` passes error events through opaquely. No UX regression, silent or otherwise.
- New test's mocks are byte-for-byte the same shape as the already-passing `/repo/app/lib/llm/streamLlm.test.ts:5-17`, and match the real export names in `cache.ts` (`computeHash`/`getCachedResult`/`setCachedResult`), `costs.ts` (`computeCost`), `persist.ts` (`appendAnalyticsEntry`). `removeCachedResult` is omitted from the cache mock but is not in `callLlm.ts`'s import graph. No mismatch.

**Candidates:**

1. `/repo/app/lib/llm/streamLlm.ts:71` — JSDoc still advertises `event: error — { error: "message", details: "..." }` but `details` is no longer emitted.
   failure_scenario: A contributor building a second SSE consumer (or extending `api.ts`) reads the protocol block as the contract, writes `setErrorBanner(\`${data.error}: ${data.details}\`)`, and ships a banner reading `"OpenRouter API error: 429: undefined"`. Nothing in CI catches it — `streamLlm.test.ts` has no assertion on the error event payload at all.

2. `/repo/app/lib/llm/streamLlm.ts:265` (helper defined at `:30`) — `errorWithDetails` now has zero readers; the OpenRouter error body is captured, attached, and then discarded.
   failure_scenario: Production streaming hits an OpenRouter 402/429/400. `errorBody` contains the actionable text ("insufficient credits", "model not found"), but the catch at `:157` logs only `message` and sends only `{ error }`. The body exists in memory and is dropped on the floor — no log, no SSE, no route handler ever sees the thrown Error (it is caught inside `streamLlm`'s own `start()`, so the "in-process consumer that opts in" named in the new JSDoc cannot exist). Root-causing a paging incident requires a code change plus redeploy.

3. `/repo/app/lib/llm/streamLlm.ts:158-162` vs `/repo/app/api/explanation/lean-error/route.ts:38`, `/repo/app/api/edit/whole/route.ts:37`, `/repo/app/api/refine/context/route.ts:54`, `/repo/app/api/edit/inline/route.ts:29`, `/repo/app/api/formalization/lean/route.ts:145`, `/repo/app/lib/formalization/artifactRoute.ts:116` — the stated rationale ("provider error bodies can echo request content, so don't send them to the client") is contradicted by six non-streaming routes that still ship the identical provider body to the HTTP client via `OpenRouterError.details`.
   failure_scenario: A privacy audit concludes provider bodies are contained because the streaming path was hardened, then finds the same OpenRouter body returned verbatim in a 502 JSON response from `/api/edit/whole`. The change buys no actual containment (the data still leaves the process on every non-streaming route) while paying the full observability cost from item 2 — a one-sided trade.

4. `/repo/app/lib/formalization/artifactRoute.ts:108` — the sibling implementation of the exact code path changed in `route.ts` still does `console.error(..., preview)` with a 500-char slice of `responseText`.
   failure_scenario: The new comment at `/repo/app/api/edit/artifact/route.ts:77-80` asserts an invariant ("shouldn't end up in server logs") that `artifactRoute.ts` — the shared handler backing the other artifact endpoints — violates on every malformed-JSON response. Whoever greps logs for user source material still finds it, and the next reader of `route.ts` trusts a guarantee the codebase does not hold.

5. `/repo/app/api/edit/artifact/route.ts:78` and `:83` — the log now carries only `responseText.length`, but line 83 still returns `responseText.slice(0, 500)` to the caller.
   failure_scenario: An operator triaging a spike of 502 `"LLM response was not valid JSON"` has `"1847 chars"` and nothing else; the malformed prefix that would identify the cause (stray prose preamble, truncated fence) is visible only to the end user, who cannot interpret or forward it. Diagnosis now depends on a user pasting a payload back into a support ticket.

6. `/repo/app/lib/llm/callLlm.test.ts:47-52` — the test exercises only `callLlm`'s Anthropic branch; `makeAnthropicClient`'s second consumer, `/repo/app/lib/llm/streamLlm.ts:207`, has no equivalent coverage, and `streamLlm.test.ts` never constructs a real client.
   failure_scenario: The per-call-construction guarantee the diff exists to establish is enforced on one of two call sites. Reintroducing a module-scope cache inside `makeAnthropicClient` would be caught, but caching the client inside `streamAnthropic` (the more natural place, since it is invoked per stream) would pass CI while reproducing the exact stale-API-key bug the rename was meant to fix.

I have everything I need. Here are my findings.

## Findings

### 1. Invalid-JSON LLM response is cached, so the 502 becomes permanent — and the new log makes it undiagnosable
**File:** `/repo/app/api/edit/artifact/route.ts` **Line:** 46 (failure surfaces at 81–85)

`callLlm` caches any non-empty `text` via `recordAndCache` (`/repo/app/lib/llm/callLlm.ts:92-94`) *before* this route validates it. The sibling implementation of this exact pattern evicts the poisoned entry — `/repo/app/lib/formalization/artifactRoute.ts:103-105` calls `removeCachedResult(cacheKey...)` in its parse-failure branch — but this route destructures only `{ text: responseText, usage }` and throws `cacheKey` away, so it can never evict.

**failure_scenario:** User POSTs `{content: "{...}", instruction: "add a node"}`; the model replies with a prose preamble before the JSON. Both `JSON.parse(cleaned)` and `JSON.parse(responseText)` throw → 502. The bad text is already in the cache under the same hash (same model/prompt/content/maxTokens). Every retry of the identical request now hits `getCachedResult` at `callLlm.ts:124`, returns the same malformed text, and 502s again — forever, with no LLM call to break the cycle. The user's only escape is changing their input. Compounding it, the reworked log at line 81 now prints only `"…invalid JSON: 4213 chars"`, so an operator reading logs cannot identify *which* cached payload is poisoned or grep for it.

---

### 2. The stated privacy rationale is inverted: content is removed from access-controlled logs but still shipped over the wire, and still logged elsewhere
**File:** `/repo/app/api/edit/artifact/route.ts` **Line:** 83

The comment says `responseText` "shouldn't end up in server logs," yet line 83 returns `responseText.slice(0, 500)` in the HTTP body — a *less* protected sink than server logs (traverses proxies, lands in browser devtools/error reporters). The same change in `/repo/app/lib/llm/callLlm.ts:186` drops `errorBody` from the log while `throw new OpenRouterError(response.status, errorBody)` keeps it flowing to clients verbatim through five handlers (`/repo/app/api/edit/whole/route.ts:37`, `/repo/app/api/edit/inline/route.ts:29`, `/repo/app/api/refine/context/route.ts:54`, `/repo/app/api/formalization/lean/route.ts:145`, `/repo/app/lib/formalization/artifactRoute.ts:116`). And the identical log statement this hunk was written to eliminate is untouched at `/repo/app/lib/formalization/artifactRoute.ts:107`, which still does `console.error(..., preview)` with a 500-char slice — that path serves most artifact endpoints, i.e. the majority of the traffic.

**failure_scenario:** Operator, believing the policy holds, ships this and stops redacting logs. A user generates a causal graph from confidential source text; the model emits malformed JSON. `/api/formalization/*` writes 500 chars of that source-derived text straight to the log at `artifactRoute.ts:107`. Net effect of the diff: zero reduction in exposure, minus the server-side debuggability for `/api/edit/artifact`.

---

### 3. `message.content[0].type` dereferences index 0 of a possibly empty array
**File:** `/repo/app/lib/llm/callLlm.ts` **Line:** 149

Unchanged line inside the touched `callLlm`, now more reachable since the hunk at line 133 sits two lines above it. `message.content` is not guaranteed non-empty.

**failure_scenario:** `callLlm({maxTokens: 8192, ...})` with an input near the context limit, or a request that stops on `max_tokens` before emitting a content block, returns `content: []`. `message.content[0]` is `undefined` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type')`. This throws *outside* the provider try/catch structure of the caller's happy path, propagating to `/repo/app/api/edit/artifact/route.ts:88`, where it is misreported to the user as `"LLM call failed: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type')"` with status 502 — an internal crash disguised as a provider error. The fix used two lines later for usage is absent here; `message.content[0]?.type === "text" ? ... : ""` would be safe.

---

### 4. OpenRouter streaming error bodies are now discarded at every sink — the only diagnostic copy is gone
**File:** `/repo/app/lib/llm/streamLlm.ts` **Line:** 265 (dead-ends at 160/162)

`errorWithDetails(...)` still attaches the provider body, but with `getErrorDetails` deleted there is now **zero** code anywhere in the repo that reads `.details` off a streaming error (confirmed by grep — the only remaining `.details` readers are `OpenRouterError` consumers on the non-streaming path). The JSDoc's claim that the property "remains attached… for any in-process consumer that opts in to reading it" describes a consumer that does not exist. Contrast the non-streaming path, which deliberately preserves the body on `OpenRouterError` and surfaces it — the two paths now behave inconsistently for the same provider failure.

**failure_scenario:** OpenRouter returns `402 {"error":{"message":"Insufficient credits, add more at ..."}}` mid-stream. `streamOpenRouter` throws with the body attached; the catch at line 157 extracts only `err.message` = `"OpenRouter API error: 402"`. Log line 160 prints that string; SSE event line 162 sends `{error: "OpenRouter API error: 402"}`; the client at `/repo/app/lib/formalization/api.ts:92` reads only `.error` and throws it. The actionable text ("insufficient credits") is now unrecoverable from any log, response, or metric — an on-call engineer sees a bare 402 with no cause. Before this diff, line 160 logged it.

---

### 5. Stale SSE protocol doc still advertises a `details` field that is no longer sent
**File:** `/repo/app/lib/llm/streamLlm.ts` **Line:** 71

```
 *   event: error   — { error: "message", details: "..." }
```
The hunk at 155–165 removed `details` from the payload but left this contract block documenting it, in a file whose *other* JSDoc was explicitly updated in the same branch (commit `f2f149b`, "tighten errorWithDetails JSDoc to describe present behavior").

**failure_scenario:** A developer adding a new SSE consumer reads this block, writes `const {error, details} = JSON.parse(dataStr)` and renders `` `${error}: ${details}` `` in an error toast. `details` is `undefined` at runtime, so users see `"OpenRouter API error: 402: undefined"` in the UI. TypeScript cannot catch this — `JSON.parse` returns `any`, and the payload has no declared type.

---

### 6. New test never restores `process.env`, and its only assertion channel is the constructor spy
**File:** `/repo/app/lib/llm/callLlm.test.ts` **Line:** 34–39 (assertion at 53)

`beforeEach` deletes both key env vars and the test body assigns `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "key-B"`, but there is no `afterEach`, no `vi.unstubAllEnvs`, and `vi.stubEnv` is not used — the fake key outlives the test. There is also no `vi.resetModules()`, so the dynamically imported `./callLlm` module instance is shared by any future test in this file. (Vitest 4's default `forks` pool with isolation confines the leak to this file today, so impact is latent rather than active — but the guard is one config change away from mattering, and the existing sibling `/repo/app/lib/llm/streamLlm.test.ts:20-23` has the same gap.) Separately, the assertion rests entirely on `constructorCalls`; `messagesCreate` is a single shared `vi.fn` assigned as an instance field, so the test never verifies the second `callLlm` actually *issued* its request through the second client.

**failure_scenario:** A developer adds a second `it()` to this file to cover the OpenRouter branch, setting only `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. `beforeEach` deletes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, so that specific ordering survives — but the moment someone adds a test that relies on the *mock* fallback while a prior test left `constructorCalls` or module state populated, or the suite is switched to `pool: 'threads'` (where Vitest shares `process.env` across workers via `SHARE_ENV`), `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="key-B"` bleeds into unrelated test files, silently routing them down the Anthropic branch at `callLlm.ts:130` against an unmocked SDK.

findings.summary: Invalid-JSON LLM responses are cached before validation and this route discards `cacheKey`, so it can never evict the poisoned entry and the 502 becomes permanent for that request.
findings.failure_scenario: The model replies with a prose preamble before the JSON; callLlm's recordAndCache (callLlm.ts:92-94) has already cached the non-empty text under the request hash. Both JSON.parse attempts fail → 502. Every retry of the identical request hits the cache at callLlm.ts:124 and returns the same malformed text without a new LLM call — forever. The sibling handler (app/lib/formalization/artifactRoute.ts:103-105) destructures `cacheKey` and calls removeCachedResult in exactly this branch; this route destructures only `{ text, usage }`. Pre-existing on main, but it sits in the catch block this diff edits, and the new length-only log removes the preview an operator would need to identify the poisoned payload.
findings.short_summary: edit/artifact never evicts poisoned cache → permanent 502

findings.summary: OpenRouter streaming error bodies are now discarded at every sink — not logged, not sent over SSE, and unreadable in-process — leaving only the bare status code for diagnosis.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenRouter returns 402 (insufficient credits), 429, or 400 (bad model slug) mid-request; these are distinguishable only by the JSON body. The throw at line 265 attaches the body as `details`, but the error is caught inside the same ReadableStream start() closure at line 156, which logs and forwards only `err.message` ("OpenRouter API error: 402"). Before this diff, the deleted getErrorDetails call logged the body. An on-call engineer now sees a bare status in logs and the browser, and recovering the cause requires shipping a code change and reproducing in production.
findings.short_summary: Streaming OpenRouter error bodies unrecoverable everywhere

findings.summary: errorWithDetails duplicates the already-imported OpenRouterError, and its new JSDoc (commit f2f149b) documents an "in-process consumer" that cannot exist because the error never escapes streamLlm's own catch.
findings.failure_scenario: The error thrown at line 265 is awaited inside start() and caught at line 156 — no code outside streamLlm can ever read `.details`, so the JSDoc's opt-in consumer is impossible by construction, and grep confirms zero readers repo-wide. The helper builds the exact message OpenRouterError's constructor produces ("OpenRouter API error: ${status}", callLlm.ts:22), so `throw new OpenRouterError(response.status, errorBody)` is a drop-in that deletes the helper, its cast, and the misleading doc — and lets a future stream error handler use the same instanceof check as the six existing route handlers.
findings.short_summary: errorWithDetails is dead weight; OpenRouterError is a drop-in

findings.summary: The SSE protocol JSDoc still documents the error event as `{ error, details }`, but line 162 now emits `{ error }` only — and this comment is the sole written spec of the wire format.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer building or extending an SSE consumer reads the protocol block and renders `${data.error}: ${data.details}` in an error banner; `details` is undefined at runtime (JSON.parse returns any, so TypeScript can't catch it), showing users "OpenRouter API error: 429: undefined". Nothing in CI catches it either — streamLlm.test.ts has no assertion on the error event payload. One-line fix: drop `, details: "..."` from the doc.
findings.short_summary: SSE doc still advertises removed `details` field

findings.summary: The log-redaction policy is half-applied: the shared handler behind six artifact endpoints still logs a 500-char slice of the LLM response, and the Anthropic streaming path leaks the provider body via err.message anyway.
findings.failure_scenario: The new comment in edit/artifact/route.ts asserts response text "shouldn't end up in server logs", but handleArtifactRoute — the higher-traffic path serving causal-graph, statistical-model, semiformal, property-tests, dialectical-map, and counterexamples — still does console.error(..., preview) with a larger slice than the one just removed. Separately, on the Anthropic path the SDK builds APIError.message from the response body (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/core/error.js makeMessage), so streamLlm's catch logs and sends that body over SSE despite the comment two lines above claiming it doesn't. A privacy audit trusting the stated invariant would find user source material in logs on the majority of routes. The fix belongs in the shared handler (e.g. one invalidJsonResponse helper used by both sites).
findings.short_summary: Redaction policy skips the shared handler + Anthropic path

findings.summary: The per-call client comment claims swapping ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the Vercel dashboard takes effect "without needing a redeploy", but Vercel injects env vars at deploy time, so running instances never see the new value.
findings.failure_scenario: During a key-rotation incident someone reads this comment, rotates the key in the Vercel dashboard, and waits for the next request to pick it up; it won't — a redeploy is required regardless of where the client is constructed, extending the outage. The new test (callLlm.test.ts:44-53) locks the mechanism in, which is fine, but the rationale should name an environment where process.env can actually change at runtime (self-hosted with runtime secret injection) or drop the claim. Per-call construction itself is harmless: measured ~2.3 µs/instance, and the SDK uses the process-global undici fetch pool, so no connection reuse is lost.
findings.short_summary: Comment's Vercel no-redeploy rotation claim is false

findings.summary: The changed streaming error payload ships with no test, while streamLlm.test.ts already exists in the same directory and covers the other stream paths.
findings.failure_scenario: streamLlm.test.ts (151 lines) asserts on sseEvent, the mock path, and the cache-hit path, but has no assertion on the error event at all — so both the shape change in this diff and any future regression (e.g. someone "restoring" details to match the stale doc) pass CI silently. CLAUDE.md's "write tests alongside implementation" was followed for callLlm.ts but not for this behavior change.
findings.short_summary: Changed SSE error payload has zero test coverage

Review complete. All eight angles finished, and I verified every candidate directly against the source before reporting — 7 findings survived, reported above.

The headline: the branch's two goals (per-call client for key rotation, log redaction) both have gaps. The redaction is only applied to one of two near-identical handlers and doesn't hold on the Anthropic path at all, and the streaming change destroys the only diagnostic copy of OpenRouter error bodies. Verification also surfaced a pre-existing correctness bug sitting in the exact catch block the diff edits: `edit/artifact` caches malformed LLM responses and can never evict them, so a bad response 502s permanently for that input. The efficiency concern about per-call client construction was measured and cleared (~2.3 µs, shared undici pool), so the mechanism is fine — only its Vercel rationale in the comment and the stale SSE protocol doc need correcting.

Dropped after verification: the altitude angle's connection-churn claim (refuted by measurement) and minor test-scaffolding duplication notes (below the reporting bar; the `beforeEach` env deletion without restore is safe under Vitest's per-file isolation, just worth knowing if the pool config ever changes).
